items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-19
items.q: And there are musicians like Bobby Hackett, for example, who's spectacular, but whose approach to music doesn't, I don't respond to emotionally at all.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. And there are musicians like Bobby Hackett, for example, who's spectacular, but whose approach to music doesn't, I don't respond to emotionally at all. It's not my kind of thing. Although I respect him and his work.
For the same reason, you don't respond to Big Spider?

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1989-08-13
items.q: I was to his house in Long Island with Bobby Hackett.

ctx.x: Yeah. About the incident with, they talked to you about it over those next three years? Oh, yeah. About the incident with Punch? Yeah.

I was to his house in Long Island with Bobby Hackett. And we talked about it then. He said, those people there, he said, I don't know what's the matter with them. But he said, but I wouldn't go back there anymore. Those are awful people. Yeah. So that was it.
When Louis came back at Zulu, Mayor Morrison gave him Keys to the City. Sure. I mean, the thing is. How do you think Morrison viewed Louis? I mean, what was his?

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: that's when I met Bobby Hackett, who played on that.

ctx.x: What were you doing with the Andrew Sisters? Uh, should I ask?

Well, all that I was doing is that, uh, somebody asked me to, uh, go up there and help out in the recording booth, because somebody who was supposed to have shown up had not. Mm-hmm. And, uh, that, that was all there was to that. I, I don't claim any, but that's the time, that's when I met Bobby Hackett, who played on that.
And what did they, you, you just were working in the booth, just doing something?
